name: Analytical meditation on emptiness
method_summary: With calm established, the practitioner examines a chosen object — the self, the body, arising, a thing — with the reasonings of the Madhyamaka (the four alternatives of arising, the fivefold or sevenfold search, neither one nor many, dependent origination) until it is not found; when nothing is found, not even non-existence, the mind rests without support in that non-finding, then analysis is resumed. Hearing and reflection precede it.
prerequisites: hearing and reflecting on the texts (three wisdoms)
signs_of_progress: joy, tears and horripilation on hearing of emptiness (MA 6.4–5)
fear of 'I am not' giving way to its end (RĀ 1.26; BCA 9.56–57)
the mind pacified without object when neither being nor non-being remains (BCA 9.35)

warnings.text: Emptiness wrongly seen destroys the slow-witted, like a snake wrongly grasped or a spell wrongly performed.
Those for whom emptiness becomes a view are incurable.
Mere absence of thought without prior analysis is like fainting and does not lead to non-conceptual wisdom.

name: The sevenfold reasoning (chariot analysis)
method_summary: The self is sought as a chariot is sought: is it other than its parts, identical with them, possessing them, in them, containing them, their collection or their shape? Not found in any of the seven ways, it is understood as a designation dependent on the aggregates, cutting the view of the transitory collection.
signs_of_progress: the view of a real self weakens; afflictions rooted in it lessen (MA 6.120)

name: Examining arising by the four alternatives
method_summary: Examining whether a thing arises from itself, from another, from both or without cause, and finding each impossible, one understands that it does not arise by own-nature (the reasoning Tibetan tradition calls the 'diamond slivers').

name: The neither-one-nor-many reasoning
method_summary: Examining whether a thing — a partless atom, a moment of consciousness, a whole — has a truly single nature or a truly manifold nature, and finding neither, one understands that it lacks own-nature, like a reflection.

name: The reasoning of dependent origination
method_summary: Because a thing arises in dependence it is empty of own-nature, and because it is empty it can arise: reflecting that nothing is not dependently arisen and so nothing is non-empty, one avoids both eternalism and annihilationism.

name: Taking the bodhisattva vow
method_summary: Before the Buddhas, following the Sugatas of old, one generates the awakening mind and undertakes to train in the bodhisattva trainings in due order; the Śikṣāsamuccaya sets out the vow (saṃvara) and the root downfalls to be avoided, drawn from the sūtras.

warnings.text: One who promises happiness to the whole world and then deceives it faces a worse destiny than one who fails to give a trifle he intended to give.

name: Generating the awakening mind
method_summary: After worship, refuge and confession, one rejoices in the virtue of all beings, requests the Buddhas to teach and not to pass away, dedicates merit, and then generates the awakening mind for the good of the world, afterwards rejoicing and inviting all beings as guests to happiness.

name: The supreme worship (sevenfold service)
method_summary: Worship of the Buddhas, the Dharma and the bodhisattvas with offerings (actual and imagined), praise and prostration, refuge, confession of faults, rejoicing in merit, requesting teaching, requesting the Buddhas to remain, and dedication — as the preparation for adopting the awakening mind.
notes: The seven-limbed form follows the Bhadracarī (src:bhadracaripranidhana); its exact division in BCA 2–3 is from memory.

name: Confession of faults
method_summary: Recalling the evil done in beginningless saṃsāra and this life, natural and prescribed faults alike, one confesses them before the Buddhas with joined palms, in fear of their result, asks that they be accepted as faults, and resolves not to do them again.

name: Dedication of merit
method_summary: The merit of practice is dedicated to the relief of all beings' sufferings and their awakening, with the aspiration to remain as long as space and the world remain and to take the world's suffering on oneself.

name: Guarding the mind with mindfulness and introspection
method_summary: Because the training cannot be kept without guarding the mind, the mind is bound with the rope of mindfulness and its states of body and mind are repeatedly examined by introspection, before acting, speaking or thinking.

name: Cultivating patience
method_summary: Seeing that anger destroys the merit of aeons, one cultivates patience by reflection: if a thing can be remedied, why be unhappy, and if not, why be unhappy; suffering has virtues (humility, compassion, dread of evil); harm arises from causes and conditions, and the enemy is a helper in the practice of patience.

name: Equalizing self and other
method_summary: One first reflects that others want happiness and fear suffering exactly as oneself, so there is no reason to protect oneself alone; the world is to be protected as one's own body with its many limbs.

name: Exchanging self and other
method_summary: Having equalized self and other, one exchanges them: seeing that all suffering comes from self-concern and all happiness from concern for others, one gives oneself to others and takes others as oneself, regarding one's former self from the standpoint of others (with envy, rivalry and pride directed at it).

equivalents.note: the Kadam mind-training practice of giving and taking develops the exchange of BCA 8

notes: Called the 'supreme secret' (paramaṃ guhyam, BCA 8.120). The detail of regarding one's old self with envy, rivalry and pride follows BCA 8.140ff (from memory).

name: Calm abiding (Kamalaśīla)
method_summary: Seated in a suitable place with a suitable posture, the practitioner fixes the mind on an object and brings it through the nine stages from placing to equipoise, remedying laziness, forgetfulness of the object, laxity and excitement, non-application and over-application by faith, aspiration, effort, pliancy, mindfulness, introspection, application and equanimity.

name: Cultivating compassion (Kamalaśīla)
method_summary: Compassion is cultivated first, seeing all beings as tormented by the three kinds of suffering: first toward those dear, then toward the indifferent, then toward enemies, until it is equal toward all beings in the ten directions and arises spontaneously.
notes: Order (friends, neutral, enemies) from memory of Bhāvanākrama I.

name: Hearing, reflection and meditation
method_summary: Wisdom from hearing grasps the meaning of scripture; wisdom from reflection discerns definitive from provisional meaning; wisdom from meditation cultivates what has been ascertained as real — so that doubt is removed and correct knowledge arises.

name: Solitude and contemplation of the body
method_summary: To settle the mind in concentration one withdraws from worldly company and discursive thought into solitude, reflects on the impermanence of loved ones and the impurity of the body to cut attachment, and on the pleasures of the forest.

name: Giving body, enjoyments and merit
method_summary: The bodhisattva mentally gives away his body, possessions and the merit of the three times to all beings, and then protects, purifies and increases them for beings' use; physical giving of the body is a matter only for those whose compassion is pure — summary only.

warnings.text: The body, which serves the true Dharma, should not be harmed for a lesser purpose; life should not be given up while the intention of compassion is impure.
If body and possessions are not protected, how can they be enjoyed by beings? What is given but cannot be used is no gift.

notes: Marked restricted because it touches on giving the body; only the texts' summary and warnings are recorded.

name: Contemplating death and impermanence
method_summary: Recollecting that death may come soon, before one's evil is exhausted, that one will go alone leaving relatives and possessions, and that the lord of death rules all who are born, one turns from craving to refuge and the Dharma.

name: Reliance on the spiritual friend
method_summary: The body is protected for beings' sake by not abandoning the spiritual friend and by constantly consulting the sūtras; the qualified student is impartial, intelligent and eager.
